entries.title: About the complete blood count
entries.text: A complete blood count (CBC) measures red cells, white cells and platelets. Values slightly outside the range are common and are not always a problem, and each lab sets its own ranges.

entries.title: Low hemoglobin
entries.text: Hemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. A level below the normal range is called anemia. Anemia has many possible causes, such as low iron, blood loss or long-term illness, so a doctor usually looks at other results and asks about symptoms before deciding what is going on.

entries.title: High hemoglobin
entries.text: A hemoglobin level above the normal range can happen with dehydration, living at high altitude, smoking or some medical conditions. A doctor can tell which one applies.

entries.title: Low red blood cell count
entries.text: Red blood cells carry oxygen. A low count often goes along with low hemoglobin and has many possible causes.

entries.title: High red blood cell count
entries.text: A high red blood cell count can be seen with dehydration or lung disease, among other causes, and needs a doctor's review.

entries.title: Hematocrit
entries.text: Hematocrit (also called PCV) is the share of your blood made up of red blood cells. It usually moves together with hemoglobin and the red cell count.

entries.title: Low MCV
entries.text: MCV is the average size of red blood cells. A low MCV means smaller than usual cells. It can be related to low iron or to inherited conditions, and doctors usually look at it together with iron tests.

entries.title: High MCV
entries.text: A high MCV means larger than usual red blood cells. It can be linked with low vitamin B12 or folate, alcohol use or some medicines, among other causes.

entries.title: MCH
entries.text: MCH is the average amount of hemoglobin in each red blood cell. It usually moves together with MCV and hemoglobin.

entries.title: MCHC
entries.text: MCHC is the concentration of hemoglobin in red blood cells. It usually moves together with MCV and hemoglobin.

entries.title: High RDW
entries.text: RDW shows how much red blood cells differ in size. A high RDW means more variation in size, and doctors read it together with the MCV.

entries.title: Low white blood cell count
entries.text: White blood cells help fight infection. A low count can be caused by viral infections, some medicines or conditions that affect the bone marrow. A doctor can judge whether it needs follow-up.

entries.title: High white blood cell count
entries.text: A high white blood cell count is common with infection or inflammation, and can also occur with stress, smoking or some medicines. A doctor can judge whether it needs follow-up.

entries.title: Low platelet count
entries.text: Platelets help blood to clot. A low count can be caused by viral infections such as dengue, by some medicines or by other conditions, and the bleeding risk depends on how low it is. Please have a doctor review it.

entries.title: High platelet count
entries.text: A high platelet count can occur after infection, with inflammation or iron deficiency, and sometimes because of bone marrow conditions. A doctor can tell which one applies.
